defects.description: The update adapter compacts a patch as a creation payload, removing explicit null before the codec can transmit a field clear.

trigger.input: timeout 30s node --input-type=module -e 'import { Service } from "./src/service.js"; const c = new Service().client(); c.create({id:"a",email:"old@example.test"}); c.update("a",{name:"Alice"}); c.update("a",{email:null}); console.log(JSON.stringify(c.read("a")));'

defects.why_missed: S9(a,d): create, update, clear, read crosses the transport boundary. The standalone creation normalizer and patch codec are correct, and each is tested, but ordinary text updates never expose their incompatible composition. A naive sparse-object oracle treats null as omission.

defects.description: CSV export removes null cells from data rows while retaining the negotiated header, shifting later fields into the wrong columns.

trigger.input: timeout 30s node --input-type=module -e 'import { Service } from "./src/service.js"; const c = new Service().client(); c.create({id:"a",name:"Alice",team:"ops"}); c.update("a",{name:"Alicia"}); console.log(JSON.stringify(c.export(["id","email","name"])));'

defects.why_missed: S9(a,d): create, update, export projects an omitted nullable field between populated columns. The naive oracle counts populated values; the protocol requires one cell per selected column. Existing CSV checks select populated columns, while codec and null-cell tests are independently green.
